ImageDescription.value:
A really beautifully kept example of this lovely 70s French car. They're not at all common anymore, and I've only seen one other in Greece so far, and it was in an awful state! Picture here: www.flickr.com/photos/92622665@N08/10312556763/in/photoli...

You've got to love how original this one is. Lovely old golden Peugeot badge on the front grille, and only one mirror on the driver's door, as was common with basic old cars. These are one of my favourite old French cars, and I just wish I could find some in France next time I visit. Do any cars in France have yellow headlights anymore? That's always the one thing I remembered of our many holidays to France as a boy.

Unfortunately it's hard to get timewarp style shots in this part of Greece, as the settlements around here have been destroyed by earthquakes in recent times, so houses are too modern.

ImageDescription.value:
An elegant Peugeot 304 Cabriolet at a private classic car meet in the grounds of Château La Borde en Sologne in Vernou-en-Sologne, France. The vehicle is presented in its factory-original Saffron Gold Metallic paint and hails from the facelift period produced from September 1972 onward, recognizable by the chrome-plated lion mounted directly onto the slats of the radiator grille.

I. Technical Development and Design Features

  • Model History & Production Run: The Peugeot 304 Cabriolet debuted in March 1970 at the Geneva Motor Show as the successor to the 204 Cabriolet. Between 1970 and 1976, only 18,647 units of this elegant open-top body variant were handcrafted at the Peugeot plant in Sochaux. The vehicle pictured documents the faithful facelift phase from September 1972 onward, where the freestanding golden lion inside the shield-shaped grille was replaced by a delicate, sculpted chrome lion without a frame, sitting directly on the black grille ripples.
  • Pininfarina's Modular Construction: Stylistically, the front fascia of the 304 was modernized and adapted to match the new family identity, borrowing the distinctive trapezoidal headlights of the larger 504 sister model. A unique characteristic of the cabriolet was its economical modular engineering: while the saloon was built on the longer standard wheelbase of 2.59 meters, the shorter cabriolet and coupe utilized the unchanged, compact rear section and passenger cabin of the predecessor 204.
  • Coachwork & Handling: To maintain the stylistic elegance of the roadster and give it sharp proportions, the vehicle was designed as a purebred two-seater. Unlike the four-door saloon, the cabriolet features a drastically shortened wheelbase of exactly 2.31 meters (a reduction of 28 centimeters). This granted the open car its sporty, compact roadster proportions and exceptionally agile, stable cornering characteristics.
  • Drivetrain & Mechanics: Underneath the hood sits the proven, transversely mounted four-cylinder all-alloy engine with an overhead camshaft, developing 65 hp from a 1,288 cc displacement in the standard version (and 74 hp with a twin-barrel carburetor in the sportier "S" variant from 1972). The fully synchronized four-speed manual transmission is located directly beneath the engine, sharing the same oil supply to save space.

II. Socio-Economic and Pop-Culture History

  • Successful Niche Strategy: During the 1970s, the European automotive market shifted drastically, and many manufacturers eliminated affordable, open-top vehicles from their lineups. Peugeot, however, masterfully occupied this niche with the 304 Cabriolet. It targeted a sophisticated, fashion-conscious, and urban clientele of the rising middle class looking for a stylish yet mechanically uncomplicated everyday cabriolet and an antidote to automotive monotony.
  • The Heritage of the Classic French Roadster: From a cultural standpoint, the 304 Cabriolet represents the final chapter of compact, lightweight French open-air motoring before the introduction of stricter international safety and crash regulations. With its refined chassis and carefree driving comfort, this saffron-gold car epitomizes French "chic" and the laid-back lifestyle of the 1970s.
